title: Induction on k, split on a negative diagonal, for Floyd-Warshall correctness
intent: Prove the main correctness theorem of the Floyd-Warshall formalisation - that fw m n k preserves canonical form and cycle-freeness on the index set {0..k} when the input m is cycle-free there - by induction on k; the step splits on whether fw m n (Suc k) has a negative diagonal entry, which decides between a negative-cycle contradiction and extending cycle-freeness one index further.
also_known_as: induction over the outer loop index

parent.name: fw_correct
parent.statement:
theorem fw_correct:
  "canonical_subs n {0..k} (fw m n k) \<and> cyc_free_subs n {0..k} (fw m n k)"
  if "cyc_free_subs n {0..k} m" "k \<le> n"

children.name: fwi_canonical_extend
children.statement:
lemma fwi_canonical_extend:
  "canonical_subs n (I \<union> {k}) (fwi m n k n n)" if
  "canonical_subs n I m" "I \<subseteq> {0..n}" "0 \<le> m k k" "k \<le> n"
children.closed_by: unfolding canonical_subs_def, apply safe; each subgoal is reduced by fwi_step' and closed by force/auto with add_mono, add_increasing and order.trans
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: one invocation of fwi extends canonicality from I to I union {k}

children.name: cyc_free_subs_diag
children.statement:
lemma cyc_free_subs_diag:
  "m i i \<ge> 0" if "cyc_free_subs n I m" "i \<le> n"
children.closed_by: instantiating the cyc_free_subs abbreviation with the empty path [] and fastforce
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: cycle-freeness on I gives a non-negative diagonal entry

children.name: fwi_cyc_free_subs'
children.statement:
lemma fwi_cyc_free_subs':
  "cyc_free_subs n (I \<union> {k}) (fwi m n k n n)" if
  "cyc_free_subs n I m" "canonical_subs n I m" "I \<subseteq> {0..n}" "k \<le> n"
  "\<forall> i \<le> n. fwi m n k n n i i \<ge> 0"
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: fwi extends cycle-freeness to I union {k} given canonicality and a non-negative diagonal

children.name: fwi_cyc_free_subs
children.statement:
lemma fwi_cyc_free_subs:
  "cyc_free_subs n (I \<union> {k}) (fwi m n k n n)" if
  "cyc_free_subs n (I \<union> {k}) m" "canonical_subs n I m" "I \<subseteq> {0..n}" "k \<le> n"
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: fwi extends cycle-freeness to I union {k} when the input is cycle-free on I union {k}

children.name: fw_neg_diag_neg_cycle
children.statement:
lemma fw_neg_diag_neg_cycle:
  "\<exists> i \<le> n. \<exists> ys. set ys \<subseteq> set xs \<union> {0..k} \<and> len m i i ys < 0" if
  "len (fw m n k) i i xs < 0" "i \<le> n" "k \<le> n" "set xs \<subseteq> {0..n}"
children.closed_by: induction on k arbitrary: i xs, using fwi_neg_cycle_neg_cycle for the base case and the step
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: a negative diagonal entry of fw implies a negative cycle

applicability.goal_shape: A conjunction P (f n k) = (canonical_subs n {0..k} (fw m n k) and cyc_free_subs n {0..k} (fw m n k)) for a recursion fw m n (Suc k) = fwi (fw m n k) n (Suc k) n n that grows the index set {0..k} by one each step; both conjuncts are abbreviations quantified over that growing set.
applicability.use_when: the recursion advances a single index k and each one-step extension is already factored into named lemmas (here fwi_canonical_extend and fwi_cyc_free_subs / fwi_cyc_free_subs'), so the base and step cases close by citing them.
applicability.avoid_when: the step needs a test that is not part of the invariant (here a negative diagonal), and the negation of that test cannot be turned into the extra hypothesis of a strengthening lemma (fwi_cyc_free_subs' takes the hypothesis 'all i <= n. fwi m n k n n i i >= 0'); then the case split will not close.

The authors state the plan the theorem follows: 'To prove the main result under the absence of negative cycles, we will proceed as follows: we show that an invocation of fwi m n k n n extends canonicality to index k, we show that an invocation of fw m n n computes a matrix in canonical form, and finally we show that canonical forms specify the lengths of shortest paths, provided that there are no negative cycles.'

The main theorem fw_correct is reused in four places after its statement: lines 1116 and 1117 derive one-conjunct lemmas from it, and lines 1290 and 1628 invoke it in later proofs (counted by grepping fw_correct over DBM/Floyd_Warshall.thy at the pinned commit).

consequences: The induction creates a base case and a step case; the step case is further split on whether there is an i <= n with fw m n (Suc k) i i < 0, whose exhaustiveness is by cases. The negative-diagonal branch needs fw_neg_diag_neg_cycle (itself proved by a second induction on k arbitrary: i xs) to contradict the input's cycle-freeness; the non-negative branch must supply the strengthened hypothesis 'all i <= n. fwi m n k n n i i >= 0' to fwi_cyc_free_subs'. The two conjuncts are proved separately (canonicality by fwi_canonical_extend, cycle-freeness by fwi_cyc_free_subs / fwi_cyc_free_subs') and only combined at the end, so each one-step invariant is stated and proved on its own.
